one_month_reasoning: No AppLovin-specific scheduled catalyst falls inside Oct 2 - Oct 31: Q3 2026 results are expected around Nov 11 (TipRanks; historically early November), and the class-action lead-plaintiff deadline is Nov 16, both outside the window. In-window items are second-order: Meta/Alphabet Q3 prints in late October (ad-market read-through, plus Meta's new AI game-creation tools), continued third-party channel checks (Edgewater, Wells Fargo pixel data) and pre-earnings analyst previews, which have leaned negative. Offsetting: the stock is at a 52-week low after a 7-session, 12% losing streak (Trefis), the company has ~$1.8bn of buyback authorization and ~$3bn cash, and short-horizon reversal after sharp selloffs is a mild tailwind. These roughly cancel, so I center the month at about today's price (median ~$282) with lognormal sigma ~20% (75% annual vol / 3.5, slightly trimmed), i.e. a near-symmetric spread.

fair_value.method: Blend of P/E (skeptic 2027E EPS $18.4 x 17x = $313, 40%), FCF yield (skeptic 2027E FCF ~$6.0bn / 330M shares = $18.2 at a 6% yield = $302, 35%) and EV/EBITDA (skeptic 2027E EBITDA $7.7bn x 13x less $0.46bn net debt / 330M = $301, 25%), giving ~$306, about 9% above the $281 close.

Current EV ~$94.7bn (281.31 x 335M + $0.46bn net debt) is ~13.9x 2026E EBITDA of ~$6.8bn (Q1+Q2 reported $3.17bn + Q3 guide midpoint $1.725bn + Q4 ~$1.9bn) and ~11.5x consensus 2027 EBITDA (~$8.2bn); 13x on my lower 2027 number is in line with Piper's multiple compression.

bear.story: Model upgrades keep slipping and gaming share saturates (Edgewater); Unity and Meta's AI game tools squeeze net-revenue spreads; e-commerce self-serve stalls (Wells Fargo pixel data); 2027 growth falls to ~10-15% and EPS ~$16; the class action or a revived regulatory/platform data-practice issue (SEC/state AG history) keeps a governance discount. 10-11x on ~$17 forward EPS.

base.story: Growth slows to ~18-20% in 2027 as gaming matures and e-commerce ramps slowly; margins stay ~80%; buybacks shrink the share count ~3%/yr; estimates drift a bit lower, then stabilize; the multiple stays de-rated at ~14-15x forward EPS (~$21 for 2028).

bull.story: The post-quarter model step-up shows up in Q3/Q4 beats, e-commerce/self-serve Axon inflects in 2027, the class action fades, and the stock re-rates to ~19-20x on ~$24-25 forward EPS, still well below the $738 high.

thesis_break_reason: At ~$205 the stock would trade at ~10-11x my already-haircut 2027 EPS and a ~9% FCF yield, with about $3bn of cash and active buybacks underneath. A price that low would most likely mean the market expects earnings to actually fall (gaming ad revenue shrinking, a platform or data-practice action by Apple/Google or regulators, or a damaging disclosure from litigation) and not just slower growth, so the base case would be broken.

reasoning: Lane: skeptic. Bear evidence collected: (1) First guidance miss since IPO in Q2 2026 (revenue 30bp, EBITDA 100bp below guide midpoint), with the CEO conceding model improvement was 'lighter than normal' and that 30-60s AI video creative is not ready. That is the core of the Feb 12 - Aug 5 class action (lead-plaintiff deadline Nov 16). (2) Downgrades: BofA to Neutral (risk to 30% LT growth), Piper to Neutral with PT $325 and multiple cut to ~18x, Wells Fargo EW $325 citing ~85% of newly added e-commerce pixel sites with no traffic, Edgewater channel checks showing stalled share-of-wallet and Q4 at +8-9% q/q. (3) Consensus 2027 EPS fell from $21.16 to $20.00 in 60 days with 19 down / 5 up revisions. (4) Heavy discretionary insider selling at $480-600 in May-June 2026 (CEO ~$51m, not under 10b5-1; director Vivas ~200k shares; CTO), plus a CTO transition on Jul 1. Weighing it honestly: the CapitalWatch money-laundering short report was retracted, the CFO says the SEC inquiry closed with no action, the 10-Q accrues no material legal loss, credit is investment grade (BBB- S&P/Fitch) with only ~$0.46bn net debt, and the business still grew 53% in Q2 at an 84% EBITDA margin. At $281 the stock trades at ~14x consensus 2027 EPS and a ~6% FCF yield, so a lot of the bear case is already priced. My fair value of ~$306 haircuts consensus 2027 EPS 8% and holds de-rated multiples. Scenarios: bear $185 (25%), base $305 (50%), bull $470 (25%); probability-weighted mean ~$319, median ~$300. Ladder: I averaged a three-scenario lognormal mixture with a single lognormal (median ~$295, sigma 0.62, below the 75% realized vol because that vol includes a one-off de-rating), which fattens the tails. Result: P(>= today's $281) about 0.55, roughly 21% chance of falling below $197 and 5% of reaching $703. Research was limited by 403 blocks on some sites (Benzinga, Invezz); I found no relevant prediction markets, and I deliberately looked up no options data.
